answer: An agent network can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a stake and earn reputation through independently verified work. New accounts receive little influence, and endorsements count only from established peers with varied interaction histories, making a fake island of agents harder to trust. The attacker must tie up capital and spend time building credible feedback; exposed coordination can cost the stake. This slows the pulse of a fake network and raises the cost of scaling it like a river of disposable accounts.
